reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer characterization of the new particles as particularly effective at binding mycobacteria is supported in the final paper by TPP-dependent bacterial affinity and the evaluation of the selected MSN-AVA-TPP formulation across infection contexts (P:S-0eca1db10f5ede6c3921; P:S-f3a48aea6adedaf97e12).

The reviewer noted that mycobacteria-directed nanoparticles had already been described. The final introduction likewise identifies prior nanoparticle-mediated M. marinum studies and prior mycobactericidal MSNs, limiting the novelty to the present functionalization and evidence package rather than the general therapeutic concept (P:S-da11d46fa2dbf5e2eb93).

The reviewer’s specific assessment of binding and in vivo activity is supported by the final paper’s bacterial-affinity experiments, reduced phagocyte internalization, and embryo bacterial-burden and survival results (P:S-0eca1db10f5ede6c3921; P:S-32648ecc7e2ab08138c0; P:S-c0c11c1b9384ba84125b).

The reviewer specifically identified the biofilm and intracellular antibacterial results. The final paper reports biofilm CFU reductions and dose-dependent intracellular-burden reductions for MSN-AVA-TPP@DOX (P:S-392fbcba982e6e198b16; P:S-0683012f85d307f67148).

The reviewer asked whether early zebrafish findings establish tolerability in mice or humans. Final evidence confines in vivo safety observations to zebrafish embryos and reports intracellular particle uptake in that model, leaving higher-organism tolerability untested (P:S-6da8028d1895b579ac04; P:S-f970cc21caeac66d5211).

The reviewer characterized the one-dose in vivo bacterial reduction as moderate. The final paper quantifies strong early one-dose reductions but also reports renewed bacterial growth, while the repeat-dose regimen is evaluated by survival rather than corresponding quantitative CFU measurements; this leaves the repeat-dose bacterial-clearance inference only partially resolved (P:S-c0c11c1b9384ba84125b; P:S-2a7b7e1fbbe5b69b7d05; P:S-2ea89fd1ab9f3d619b49).

The reviewer requested clarification of the intended route and justification of the zebrafish model. The final paper supports a proposed local-treatment use while its embryo efficacy protocol administers treatment into the caudal vein, so direct evidence for local delivery remains outstanding (P:S-659bd52c3fc53d33dcf4; P:S-f970cc21caeac66d5211).

Audit-only resolution of the nanoparticle-size and medium-characterization concern. The final paper reports mean-size measurements in water and DMEM with 10% FBS, independent runs, and accompanying physicochemical characterization (P:S-6c6c072c658cc0bc6099; P:S-80f19f3e2f960f970eb7).

Audit-only resolution of the flow-cytometry display concern. The final Figure 2 legend specifies histograms generated on fluorescent bacterial populations and refers to the gating strategy (P:S-7fcaad58f470ce0d2a4e).

Audit-only resolution of the request for additional antibiotics and mycobacterial species. The final paper reports clarithromycin loading and M. fortuitum in vitro and embryo testing (P:S-b7a7f4cc7dd68b41d73c; P:S-a89d135e7c08ec7d4e9f).

Audit-only resolution of the technical-replicate concern. The final figure legends document three biological replicates for the affinity experiment and four biological replicates with at least two technical replicates for the biofilm experiment (P:S-7fcaad58f470ce0d2a4e; P:S-2a7b7e1fbbe5b69b7d05).

Audit-only resolution of the dose-comparison concern. The final intracellular assay includes matched theoretical free-DOX concentrations, and the zebrafish protocol specifies the 500-pg free-DOX comparator (P:S-b3dae0d1fe377cea8002; P:S-f970cc21caeac66d5211).
Audit-only resolution of the requested prior-work overview. The final introduction identifies prior mycobactericidal MSN examples and their payload classes (P:S-da11d46fa2dbf5e2eb93).

Audit-only resolution of the request to test whether DOX-loaded MSN-AVA-TPP blocks phagocyte uptake. The final paper reports reduced M. marinum internalization for both empty and DOX-loaded nanosystems in MDM and MoDC (P:S-7e999b5f5a99725d1e20; P:S-b3dae0d1fe377cea8002).

limiting_points.text: The contribution is differentiated by its formulation and evidence package, but not by the general premise of nanoparticle-mediated antimycobacterial treatment: prior nanoparticle studies and prior mycobactericidal MSNs are already identified.

supporting_points.text: The specific contribution is a TPP-functionalized MSN platform selected for M. marinum affinity and then evaluated after doxycycline loading across planktonic, biofilm, intracellular, and zebrafish infection settings.

questions.text: How does efficacy, distribution, and safety after local delivery to a cutaneous lesion or granuloma compare with the intravenous caudal-vein administration used in the embryo model?

strengths.text: The evidence links bacterial-surface affinity to reduced uptake by human phagocytic cells and to reduced bacterial burden with improved survival in infected zebrafish embryos.
The study tests the loaded nanosystem in biofilms and infected macrophage-like cells, with quantitative reductions in bacterial burden beyond the clinically referenced free-DOX condition.

summary.text: This review concerns TPP-functionalized mesoporous silica nanoparticles loaded with doxycycline for M. marinum. The final paper supports activity from bacterial affinity through biofilm and intracellular assays to infected zebrafish embryos. The main residual limits are the restricted translational safety evidence, the absence of repeat-dose quantitative CFU data, and the lack of direct local-delivery testing despite a local-treatment framing.

weaknesses.text: The zebrafish embryo findings do not establish tolerability, biodistribution, or safety in higher organisms; the in vivo safety evidence remains confined to the embryo model.

The repeat-dose regimen improves embryo survival, but its bacterial-clearance claim is not matched by quantitative CFU measurements under those repeat-dose conditions; the one-dose data also show later bacterial regrowth.
